newsitem.title: spain: ALBANIA UNDER-21 TEAM MULLS ASYLUM BID - PLAYER.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIA UNDER-21 TEAM MULLS ASYLUM BID - PLAYER.

text.p: A member of Albania's under-21 soccer squad said on Wednesday he and his teammates want to stay in Spain after playing two matches here and will soon decide whether to seek asylum.

"It's true we want to stay here. But we still don't know what we will do. We will decide tonight or tomorrow morning," Albanian under-21 player Zeka Kresnic told Reuters. He was speaking while watching Albania's national team play Germany in Granada.
A pair of home matches for Albania's national team and two games for its under-21 squad were moved to Spain because of political unrest and violence sweeping the players' homeland.

The 20-man national team, which had World Cup European group qualifier matches in Granada against Ukraine and Germany, was drawn from Albanians playing for foreign clubs mostly in Greece, Germany, Slovenia, Croatia, Romania and Malta.
But the under-21 squad was assembled from teams in the Albanian soccer league. The players and their coaches were reportedly scheduled to fly home to Albania on Thursday.
But some of the under-21 players were apparently having second thoughts. "We would like to stay here in Spain." Kresnic said. "We cannot play in Albania. We hope to be signed by teams."
Asked about a news report that members of his team had contacted Spanish human rights groups, Kresnic said: "I hope it's true. I heard something about it."
Albania's under-21 team fared poorly in its Spanish matches, losing 0-4 to Germany on Tuesday and 0-3 against Ukraine last Saturday.
Albania's national team also suffered two defeats. It was beaten 2-3 by Germany on Wednesday and 0-1 by Ukraine last Saturday.
